title: He looked up—and chose what looked like heaven.
paragraphs: He looked up—and chose what looked like heaven.
But it was leading him straight to hell.
In Genesis 13, Lot had a choice. Two lands. Two futures. Two destinies.
Green. Watered. Prosperous. It looked like the garden of the Lord.
Quick decision. Sharp eyes. Business mindset.
Scripture whispers it softly: he pitched his tents toward Sodom.

Toward compromise.
Toward corruption.
Toward a city already rotting with sin.

First, he looked.
Then he leaned.
Then he lived there.

It never starts loud.
It starts logical.
And Lot still thought he was right.

Family shattered.
Wife turned to ash.
Legacy reduced to grief.
All because what looked good wasn’t God.

But because Abraham interceded…
and because God is rich in mercy.
That’s the Gospel thread right there.
We’ve all chosen “well-watered plains” that pulled us away from God.
We’ve trusted our eyes more than His voice.

Not to affirm our choices,
but to rescue us from them.

Even when you choose wrong,
grace can still find you.
It doesn’t excuse staying in Sodom.
So if you’re standing in a “good-looking” decision right now…

Ask:
Is this drawing me closer to God—or just deeper into comfort?
Because not every open door is from Him.
And not every blessing is safe.
